question: Which of the following is NOT subject to dissolution?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Legislative Council**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Legislative Council is a permanent body and is not subject to dissolution.
 
• The members of the Legislative Council have a term of 6 years, and 1/3rd of its members retire every 2 years.
 
• It functions as the upper house in the states that have a bicameral legislature.
 
• Examples of Indian states with a Legislative Council include Bihar, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Telangana, and West Bengal.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cabinet**

 
 
• The Cabinet is a group of senior ministers chosen by the Prime Minister. It is subject to dissolution as it functions as long as it enjoys the confidence of the Lok Sabha.
 
• It is a part of the executive branch of the government and is responsible for making policy decisions and ensuring their implementation.
 
 
 
• **Legislative Assembly**
 
 
• The Legislative Assembly is the lower house of the state legislature in a bicameral system or the sole house in a unicameral system.
 
• It is subject to dissolution, typically once every 5 years, or earlier if the government loses the majority.
 
 
 
• **Council Of Ministers**
 
 
• The Council of Ministers is headed by the Prime Minister at the central level and the Chief Minister at the state level.
 
• It is subject to dissolution and functions as long as it enjoys the confidence of the Lok Sabha or the State Legislative Assembly.
